newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai sets conditions for supermarket entry.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai sets conditions for supermarket entry.

text.p: Shanghai is setting conditions for foreign entrants into its booming supermarket sector and wants them to offer large-scale or specialised services, industry officials said on Thursday.
Shanghai has more than 760 supermarkets, up from eight in 1991, with turnover in the first half of 1996 of 2.1 billion yuan ($253 million), against 2.4 billion in all 1995, official figures show.
The city expects to have 800 by the end of this year and 1,500, with turnover of more than 10 billion yuan, by 2000, according to official projections.
This boom has attracted foreign firms such as Yaohan International Holding, Daiei, Carrefour and Dutch retailer Ahold, which announced a joint venture this month with Shanghai Zhonghui Supermarket.
"It will be hard for new foreign firms to enter the market now," said Shen Huijian, vice manager of Shanghai Zhonghui.
"The possibility of new approval is small," she said in an interview. "Some Chinese companies in this sector are very nervous (about more foreign competition)."

An official of the Shanghai city Commerce Commission said that it would strictly control foreign investment in small and medium-size supermarkets but welcomed investment in large-scale or specialised supermarkets and shopping malls.
"The Carrefour store in Shanghai has 6,000 square metres," he said. "In France, it would have 10-20,000 square metres."

"The foreign investment in this sector has brought in capital, technology and management," he said. "But we will not approve projects similar to those already here. We must protect the profits of existing investors.
"We want competition but not excess competition," he said.
Shen said Zhonghui chose Ahold over other prospective foreign partners in part because of its expertise in fresh food, an area in which Zhonghui expects to beat its competitors.

The joint venture will invest $50 million to upgrade Zhonghui's existing 15 supermarkets and expand to 100 outlets by the year 2000, she said. She estimated 1996 turnover at 150 million yuan, up from 140 million in 1995.

The firm will choose new sites in areas poorly served by supermarkets or in new suburban districts being built to house hundreds of thousands of city residents who are being relocated as part of a giant urban redevelopment plan, she said.

Industry analysts say that this redevelopment is a major factor for the rapid growth in supermarket business, giving supermarkets a chance to establish themselves in areas not served by existing shops.
Other factors are low prices, the convenience of buying many goods under the same roof and the faster pace of life, forcing people to buy goods more quickly than their parents did.

Market leader Shanghai Hualian Supermarket Co, a unit of Shanghai Huilian, announced on Tuesday that it had opened its 100th supermarket. It has 68 in Shanghai and 32 in neighbouring provinces and cities.
So far this year, it has posted sales of 700 million yuan, a record for such a period and expects the figure to reach 900 million for the full year, a company official said.
